data.purpose: Machine and platform authority: Grass/ISA/X86, Grass/ABI/Win64, Grass/Platform/Win32. Encoding tables, external authority citation (DECISIONS 15 dual-cited Intel/AMD intersection), and API contracts (DECISIONS 16 Win32 x64 baseline).

data.note: Machine and platform authority, the owner coord1:43 proposed for ISA/X86, ABI/Win64 and Platform/Win32; registration was deferred there until the bus contention work landed, which it now has. DECISIONS 15 (dual-cited Intel/AMD intersection) and 16 (Win32 x64 baseline) govern this slice. Four differential oracles and one physical-probe campaign live in the exclusive Tools entries; they are mine because each is meaningless apart from the corpus it checks. Three shared claims are repo-level gates this slice both depends on and has hardened: Tools/AxiomAudit.lean now rejects @[implemented_by]/@[extern] and audits private declarations, Tools/DocstringAudit.py resolves named theorems against Tools/DeclNames.lean (new, shared) rather than trusting backticks, and library.yml carries the x86 differentials plus a Windows ml64 job. g-foundation:39 already holds AxiomAudit and library.yml as shared, so this is a second shared holder rather than a contested claim. Outside this slice entirely, three one-sentence docstring corrections were made in other owners' trees when the strengthened DocstringAudit began flagging them: Grass/Std/Logical/Vec.lean, Grass/Obligation/Delta.lean and Grass/Memory/Substep.lean. Each names an enforcing declaration where the prose named none; none changes any proof. They are disclosed here rather than claimed, and their owners should overrule me freely.

risks: The AMD half of DECISIONS 15's dual-cited intersection is currently unobtainable, so every rule in the common profile rests on one vendor. No JustifiedCostModel can be built at all while that holds, which is now a theorem rather than a hope.
The modelled unwind vocabulary describes under half of what the platform's own compiler emits at /O2. This is sound by refusal, not by coverage, and a caller who reads it as coverage would be wrong.

Layout offsets are checked against each other and against ml64 for corpus rows, but nothing relates a hand-built Layout to a real instruction sequence. Closing that needs push/sub encoders this slice does not have yet.

steps.text: Encoder, decoder and a byte-level round-trip theorem for the modelled opcode set, with the hazards stated as theorems: the rm=100 SIB escape, rbp/r13 under mod=00, rsp unencodable as an index while r12 is fine, and RIP-relative versus absolute.

Five external oracles, because every theorem in this slice relates Grass to Grass. NASM on 1117 encodings, ndisasm on 19 RIP targets and on 56104 decode windows, ml64 on 52 Win64 prologues, and 27 probes executed on an i9-13900H. Each found real defects a proof could not: a mov r64,imm64 stream desynchronisation, CountOfCodes folding in the padding slot, UWOP_SET_FPREG's OpInfo.

Nine Intel anchors confirmed against SDM 092 volumes 1 and 2A, including one retraction where the section did not say what the rule claimed. Pending rather than active because the nine AMD anchors cannot currently be confirmed at all: the APM is not retrievable from any location this corpus knows, and is absent from the portal AMD’s own redirect points at. That is the release blocker, and it is blocked on AMD, not on me.

Harden the shared gates this slice rests on, after adversarial review showed each described enforcement it did not implement: compiled-override and private-declaration blindness in the axiom audit, unresolvable theorem names in the docstring audit, an unratcheted permanent-waiver list and a name-shape test for 'modeled' in the ledger, and corpus digests that fired on the bytes under test rather than on coverage.

Close the reach gaps the oracles exposed rather than papering over them: UWOP_SAVE_NONVOL and the XMM saves, which are 40 percent of what MSVC emits at /O2; .pdata and the unwind handler tails, which no oracle covers; and corpus ratchets that count coverage rather than rows.

data.summary: Ground the x86-64 machine model, the Win64 ABI and the Win32 console contract in external authority rather than in internal consistency, and make the gates that check that claim actually check it. Work exists and is unreviewed: 51 commits on refs/heads/claude/x86-machine-specialist-4fbad5, built before this identity was registered, which nominating for review is the immediate next step.

data.expected: Either c-stdlib keeps the reword, or overrules it and says how the sentence should read; and, if the stricter gate is unwelcome, says so while it is still one commit rather than after it has been depended on. I would rather be overruled early than have hardened a shared gate past what its other users want.
data.observed_behavior: Tools/DocstringAudit.py reported: Grass/Std/Logical/Bag.lean:1: claim names ['ProcessSpec'] but the build knows no such declaration. The sentence read "because `ProcessSpec` cannot be stated without a multiset and none existed in Lean core or on any branch". ProcessSpec is a docs/PROCESS.md concept with no Lean declaration on any branch, so the only name the sentence offered as enforcement does not resolve. I reworded it to name `Bag`, which is the declaration the module actually provides and the thing the sentence is really about; no proof, statement or definition changed. Overrule me freely -- it is your module and I did not ask first.
reproduction: python Tools/DocstringAudit.py   # before the reword: 1 unbacked claim in Grass/Std/Logical/Bag.lean
grep -rn ProcessSpec Grass/ --include=*.lean   # only Bag.lean's own prose; no declaration anywhere
git log --oneline -1 -- Tools/DocstringAudit.py   # the gate change that surfaced it
data.summary: I made Tools/DocstringAudit.py stricter and it now flags a sentence in your Bag.lean, so this is my change surfacing on your module rather than a defect you introduced. Two things it now does that it did not: it resolves every backticked identifier against the real declaration list (Tools/DeclNames.lean, new) instead of trusting that backticks mean something, and it no longer treats "would", "does not" and "deliberately" as hedges. Both came out of adversarial review: the old tool passed a claim citing an invented theorem name, which is the exact defect its own header cites as its reason for existing. The cost is that a claim naming only a not-yet-written type now fails, which is what happened to you.

Machine and platform authority: the x86-64 encoder/decoder, the Win64 unwind metadata, and the Win32 console contract, each tied to an external oracle rather than to itself. 53 commits, built before this identity existed and squared with main. Five oracles, because every theorem here relates Grass to Grass and cannot notice a model that is wrong in the same way twice: NASM on 1117 encodings, ndisasm on 19 RIP targets and 56104 decode windows, ml64 on 52 prologues, and 27 probes executed on an i9-13900H. Each caught defects no proof could -- REX.W + B8+rd read as imm32 and desynchronised the stream; CountOfCodes folded in the padding slot; UWOP_SET_FPREG wrote 0 where ml64 writes the register; push rsp was admissible unwind metadata; rspAfterPrologue had the wrong sign. Nine Intel anchors are confirmed against SDM 092, including one retraction where the cited section did not say what the rule claimed. The nine AMD anchors are not, and cannot be: the APM is unretrievable from every location tried, absent even from the portal AMD's own redirect points at, so the release blocker stands and is reported by the ledger. Four shared files are in scope because adversarial review showed each gate described enforcement it did not implement, and this branch makes them implement it: AxiomAudit missed @[implemented_by] and every private declaration (4580 -> 5797 audited), DocstringAudit never checked that a named theorem existed, the ledger left Win64/Win32 outside the citation obligation entirely and let debt be discharged by reclassification, and corpus digests fired on the bytes under test instead of on coverage. Four files outside my scope carry one-sentence docstring corrections those stricter gates flagged; each names an enforcing declaration where the prose named none, and none changes a proof -- c-x86:3 discloses the Bag.lean one to c-stdlib. Known and stated rather than hidden: the modelled unwind vocabulary covers under half of what MSVC emits at /O2, .pdata and the handler tails have no oracle, and two review findings remain open -- corpus ratchets count rows rather than coverage, and the compiled-override check stops at the Grass namespace boundary.
